rows.citation: Nandi A, Chartrand T, Van Geit W, et al. (2022). Single-neuron models linking electrophysiology, morphology, and transcriptomics across cortical cell types. Cell Reports 40(6): 111176.
rows.model_type: Morphologically detailed all-active conductance-based mouse visual cortex neuron models (BluePyOpt/NEURON-style optimisation), fitted to 230 Allen patch-clamp experiments
rows.controlled_mutations: no - models are fitted to data; conductance perturbations (about 10%) are used for Sobol sensitivity analysis, not as seeded faults to detect.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - experimental step, ramp and coloured-noise protocols; models fitted on DC steps and checked on further DC steps and noise.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - fitted on electrophysiological E-features using BluePyOpt and eFEL; spike-time explained variance used for noise responses.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - fixed experimental stimulus battery; training objectives chosen by staged workflow design, not searched for detection power.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - models evaluated on stimuli withheld from optimisation (extra DC steps, coloured noise); a 70/30 split is used only for a classifier; no held-out fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models or code.
rows.software: All-active-Workflow https://github.com/AllenInstitute/All-active-Workflow (built on BluePyOpt; eFEL listed in resources)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Nandi builds and validates data-fitted models against experiments. NeuroSem would compare an edited model with its own reference across a selected battery to detect single-fault changes; it could draw on such models if NeuroML versions and licences allow.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, 15 authors, Cell Reports 40(6) 111176, Aug 2022); Europe PMC REST search (abstract, PMID 35947954, PMC9793758); Europe PMC fullTextXML (STAR Methods: protocols, validation stage, noise generalisation, key resources, GitHub URL); GitHub REST API for repo existence.

rows.citation: Komendantov AO, Venkadesh S, Rees CL, et al. (2019). Quantitative firing pattern phenotyping of hippocampal neuron types. Scientific Reports 9: 17915.
rows.model_type: No computational neuron models; classification of published experimental firing responses of rodent hippocampal neuron types (Hippocampome.org)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - analyses digitised experimental recordings; no models are edited or perturbed.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - uses suprathreshold step-current pulses of varied amplitude and duration from literature; only depolarizing steps, not a designed battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - first-spike delay, normalised ISIs, post-firing silence and slow-wave amplitude feed objective rules classifying transient and steady-state firing patterns.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no stimulus or protocol selection; classification criteria are fixed.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - clustering of pattern phenotypes and statistical associations; no train/test split reported.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models or code.
rows.software: none as a package; firing-pattern parameters, spike times and analysis scripts released via Hippocampome.org (per abstract; not separately inspected)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Offers a rule-based firing-pattern taxonomy NeuroSem could adapt for its qualitative firing-regime feature. It does not test models, edits or protocols; NeuroSem would add fault detection and battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, 6 authors, Sci Rep 9, article 17915, 2019-11-29, CC BY 4.0); Europe PMC REST search (abstract, PMID 31784578, PMC6884469); Europe PMC fullTextXML (methods: data sources, extracted parameters, SPSS clustering, MATLAB).

rows.citation: Beck J, Deistler M, Bernaerts Y, et al. (2022). Efficient identification of informative features in simulation-based inference. arXiv preprint arXiv:2210.11915.
rows.doi: unverified (no DOI in arXiv abs page metadata; arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2210.11915 resolved via OpenAlex)
rows.model_type: Single-compartment Hodgkin-Huxley model (Pospischil-type with M and L currents) plus a linear Gaussian toy model; simulation-based Bayesian inference
rows.controlled_mutations: no - parameters sampled from a prior to train a likelihood estimator; no seeded faults or edited model variants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - the HH simulations appear to use a single stimulus; no multi-protocol battery described in the text read.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - 10 electrophysiology summary features (e.g. spike count, latency, AP amplitude/width, AHP, adaptation, resting potential) extracted with the Allen SDK.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - greedy selection of informative features, compared with random feature orderings; selects features, not stimulation protocols, for inference rather than fault detection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - posterior accuracy checked against brute-force re-estimation and analytic ground truth; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models or code (neural density estimators are used as a method).
rows.software: fslm_repo https://github.com/berenslab/fslm_repo (URL stated in the arXiv PDF; built on the sbi library; repository not inspected, GitHub API rate-limited)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Beck ranks features by posterior-uncertainty reduction for parameter inference, with greedy versus random comparison. NeuroSem would greedily select stimulation protocols by mutant coverage, with calibrated tolerances and held-out models.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abs page HTML (citation meta tags: title, 5 authors, 2022-10-21; abstract); arXiv PDF v2 text via pypdf (methods, HH model, features, greedy selection, code URL); OpenAlex (arXiv record only, no published version found). Semantic Scholar API returned 429; arXiv export API returned empty.

rows.citation: Kreuz T, Chicharro D, Houghton C, et al. (2013). Monitoring spike train synchrony. Journal of Neurophysiology 109(5): 1457-1472.
rows.model_type: Spike-train dissimilarity measures (improved and real-time SPIKE-distance); applied to recorded seizure spike trains and model EEG, not neuron models
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no model variants; measures compare observed spike trains.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - no stimulation protocols; analyses spike trains and continuous signals.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - uses spike timing via parameter-free time-resolved distances rather than electrophysiology features such as rheobase or AP shape.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no protocol or test selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - demonstrations on example field and model data; no held-out evaluation design.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models or code.
rows.software: unverified (publisher full text blocked; abstract read only)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: SPIKE-distance offers an alternative way to compare reference and edited spike outputs. NeuroSem would use interpretable per-protocol features with refinement-calibrated tolerances; spike distances could be a justified secondary metric or ablation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, 5 authors, J Neurophysiol 109(5) 1457-1472, 2013-03-01); Europe PMC REST search (abstract, PMID 23221419, no PMC full text). Publisher page journals.physiology.org returned HTTP 403 (bot challenge).

rows.citation: Tripathy SJ, Savitskaya J, Burton SD, et al. (2014). NeuroElectro: a window to the world's neuron electrophysiology data. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 8: 40.
rows.model_type: Literature-mined database of neuron electrophysiological properties (not models); Python library, REST API and web application
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no models or perturbations; text-mining and curation of published measurements.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - aggregates reported property values; no stimulation of models.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - catalogues properties such as input resistance, resting potential and spike amplitude under a purpose-built electrophysiology ontology.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - text-mining concept matching validated on a manually curated sample of 279 articles; unrelated to model testing.
rows.ai_transformations: no - uses text-mining and fuzzy string matching, not AI-edited models or code.
rows.software: NeuroElectro https://github.com/neuroelectro/neuroelectro (URL stated in paper; GitHub API reports the repo moved, target not resolved due to rate limit)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: NeuroElectro supplies experimental reference values for testing models against data; it mentions early SciUnit-based model testing. NeuroSem compares an edited model with its own reference model, so it needs no experimental database.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, 5 authors, Front Neuroinform 8, 2014-04-29); Europe PMC REST search (abstract, PMID 24808858, PMC4010726); Europe PMC fullTextXML (validation sample, SciUnit mention, code URL, CC BY 3.0).

rows.citation: Davison AP, Brüderle D, Eppler J, et al. (2009). PyNN: a common interface for neuronal network simulators. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 2: 11.
rows.model_type: Simulator-independent Python API for spiking network models (standard point-neuron cell types, some multicompartment support) across NEURON, NEST, PCSIM, Brian and neuromorphic hardware
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no seeded faults; compares simulators and initial conditions for one network example.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - examples use network activity and offset currents, not a stimulation battery for single-neuron behaviour.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - compares membrane traces and network activity across NEURON and NEST; no standardised single-neuron feature set.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no protocol or test selection.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models or code.
rows.software: PyNN https://github.com/NeuralEnsemble/PyNN (paper states CeCILL licence in 2009; current GitHub API licence field NOASSERTION, so current licence unverified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: PyNN enables running one model on several simulators and argues cross-checking catches simulator bugs. NeuroSem would quantify behavioural preservation after edits or translation with calibrated multi-protocol tests; PyNN is relevant to the optional cross-simulator arm.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, container, DOI; lists only Davison AP and issued year 2008); Europe PMC REST search (8 authors, pubYear 2009, PMID 19194529, PMC2634533, abstract); Europe PMC fullTextXML (NEURON vs NEST comparison, CeCILL licence); OpenAlex (Davison only); GitHub REST API (repo exists).

notes: PyNN year conflict: Crossref issued = 2008 (journal volume 2 year) while Europe PMC pubYear = 2009 and PMC copyright line reads 2009; the DOI suffix contains 2008.
